name: Domizerka
description: Domizerka is a western domino connecting game played by matching open ends on a shared layout and managing hand exit routes through careful pip coverage.

overview.description: Domizerka is a western domino connecting game played by matching open ends on a shared layout and managing hand exit routes through careful pip coverage.

history.origins: The game is encountered as a named connecting domino ruleset in modern rules references and social domino play communities.
timeline: Modern era: circulated as a distinct named connecting domino format.
history.cultural: Played as an approachable social domino game with simple legality and strategic end management.
history.evolution: Core matching structure is stable; table policies vary around draw and scoring handling.

setup.dealing: Deal tiles by player count; remaining tiles may form a boneyard depending on table profile.
setup.equipment: Dominoes and table space; optional score tracking.

rules.objective: Be first to empty your hand, or minimize remaining pips in a blocked finish.
rules.gameplay: Players place legal matching tiles to open ends of the layout. If blocked, the active table profile determines draw or pass handling. The hand ends when a player goes out or all players are blocked.
keyRules: One tile is normally played per turn.
Blocked turns resolve via draw-or-pass profile.
Hand ends on first-out or full block resolution.

strategy.basic: Keep multiple pip values available to respond to changing ends.
strategy.intermediate: Track scarce values to avoid committing into dead tiles.
strategy.advanced: Control end values while preserving your own safe exits.
tips: Do not burn your only connector for a common end value early.
Late hand, prioritize guaranteed plays over risky end shaping.

synthesis.shortDescription: Domizerka is a named connecting domino game on a double-6 set, focused on matching play, end management, and safe hand exits.
